documents.title: User stories — Model and contracts (T0)
documents.body:
# User stories — Model and contracts (T0)

## Personas

- **The programme owner** — approves V2's organisational model and the tranche-0 T0 gate; the project re-closes on that approval.
- **The tenant admin** — creates industries and departments, curates the job catalogue, publishes and retires releases, and creates and retires bindings.
- **The job author** — writes the job anatomy (charter, capability, procedure reference, model reference, recipe, knowledge pins, memory, tool grants, limits, gates, authority) that a release freezes.
- **The run caller** — names a binding when creating a run; a retired or unpinned binding must be refused, not honoured.
- **The executor author** — adds an executor kind as an implementation plus an enum value, never as a branch in the run path (D61).
- **The T2 owner** — consumes the decision-ladder schema and contracts; evaluation behaviour is T2's, not T0's.
- **The delivery leads of T1, T2 and T3** — blocked by T0; the organisation spine is their prerequisite (SPEC §12).
- **The design-site reader** — reads the Organisation page with its live rows and LIVE ribbon.

## Stories

- As the programme owner, I want the organisational model approved and the spine shipped first, so that T1–T3 start on real rows and no concept has two stores (D40).
- As a tenant admin, I want `industries.create` and an ordered `department` tree, so that the organisation is tenant-scoped rows rather than fixtures.
- As a job author, I want a `job_catalogue` and an immutable `job_release` with a SHA-256 release hash, so that a published release cannot be rewritten by an application bug.
- As a tenant admin, I want a `job_binding` that pins exactly one release hash and one executor kind, so that a run executes a known, frozen job.
- As a run caller, I want a run on a retired or mismatched binding refused `409 job_binding_stale` before any model call, so that stale work neither executes nor spends.
- As an executor author, I want one internal `Executor` contract with an extensible `executor_kind`, so that a new kind is an implementation plus an enum value, not a branch through the run path.
- As the T2 owner, I want the decision-ladder types as schema and contracts only, so that T2 evaluates them without a second store.
- As a design-site reader, I want the Organisation page to render the live rows with a LIVE ribbon, so that the published surface is inspectable and unwired sections stay DESIGN.

## Scenarios

- Given a fresh database, when migrations run, then `industry`, `job_catalogue`, `job_department`, `job_release` and `job_binding` exist with FORCE RLS and tenant policies, `department` carries `industry_id`, `ordinal` and `is_primary`, and `run.job_binding_id` and `run.release_hash` are nullable.
- Given the embedded migration list, when it is read, then it carries `(40, "organisation")` — the next free number moved to 40 when `0039_document_outputs.sql` took 39.
- Given one job placed in two departments, when the join rows are read, then the ordinals are contiguous from 1 and exactly one placement is primary.
- Given the same job and pins compiled twice, when the release hash is computed, then the hashes are identical and the snapshots byte-identical — explicit recursive key sort, then SHA-256.
- Given a retired binding, when `runs.create` names it, then the response is `409 job_binding_stale`, it names the binding's release hash and the requested one, and no `run` or `job` row is written.
- Given an active binding, when a run names it with its pinned release, then the run records `job_binding_id` and `release_hash`; an internal-agent binding also records its pinned agent.
- Given a job with no capability, agent or procedure, when a binding is created, then it is refused `422`; given a viewer, when `job_releases.publish` is invoked, then it is `403` and no release row is written.
- Given a test-only third executor kind, when it registers, then a run resolves it without editing the run path.
- Given one tenant, when `migrate --seed` runs twice, then the three industries, the five ordered departments and the job rows exist once and the second run changes no row.
- Given a seeded tenant, when `conveyor snapshot` runs, then `organisation.json` carries the industries, departments, jobs, releases and bindings and no secret value or email.
- Given the live design site, when the Organisation page loads, then it renders the live rows and the ribbon shows LIVE, while unwired sections keep DESIGN.

## Verify

- `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test organisation` — schema and RLS, department ordering, release-hash determinism, binding/executor agreement, the retired-pin refusal, the third-kind registration and the seed.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test organisation_gate` — the 409 before the insert, the pin recording, and the 422/403 refusals.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test registry --test parity_http_mcp` — every organisation action served over HTTP and MCP and matching `served-spec.lock.json`.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test snapshot_deterministic organisation_is_populated_for_a_seeded_tenant` — `organisation.json` populated for a seeded tenant.
- `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs` — the design data matches the snapshot.
- `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project T0` — the acceptance manifest `acceptance/programme/T0.toml`.

## Links

- Issue: #34; PR #65 (merged `1f48e2685e333ef2f6704e677afaae9f80e664f1`, 2026-11-14).
- Spec: `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §4.1–§4.6, §10.3–§10.5, §12 T0; decisions D38, D40, D60, D61.
- Design source: `docs/design/v2.js` F.industries/departments/jobs/releases/bindings (#32, closed).
- Code: `migrations/0040_organisation.sql`, `crates/domain/src/executor.rs`, `crates/store/src/organisation.rs`, `crates/actions/src/organisation.rs`, `seed/organisation.json`.
- Record: `docs/evidence/rework/T0.json`; `acceptance/programme/T0.toml`.

## Notes

Reconstructed from the issue, the merged PR and the programme record on 2026-11-28 for standard v4. T0 closed on 2026-11-14 and the project re-closed green at snapshot `7f0df874e7c26681ee36923b5c17e76a99254b24` on 2026-11-26. This is the Delivery narrative the standard asks for, not a new claim.

documents.title: Acceptance criteria — Model and contracts (T0)
documents.body:
# Acceptance criteria — Model and contracts (T0)

## Scenarios

- The SPEC §12 T0 acceptance holds: a job is created in the conveyor, a release is published, a binding pins its hash, a run on a retired binding refuses `409 job_binding_stale`, no concept has two stores, and a test-only third executor kind registers without editing the run path.
- `migrations/0040_organisation.sql` creates `industry`, `job_catalogue`, `job_department`, `job_release` and `job_binding` with FORCE RLS and tenant policies; `department` gains `industry_id`, `ordinal` and `is_primary`; `run.job_binding_id` and `run.release_hash` are nullable and shape-checked.
- `job_release.release_hash` is SHA-256 over the canonical snapshot (explicit recursive key sort), stored under a 64-character lowercase-hex shape check; the frozen hash and snapshot cannot be rewritten.
- `job_binding` pins one release hash and one `executor_kind`; the kind is an open slug with no value check because the code registry is the authority, and `retired_at` ends its life.
- A retired or mismatched binding is refused before the insert: `RunStoreError::JobBindingStale` maps to `409 job_binding_stale`, the refusal names both hashes, and no `run` or `job` row is written.
- An active binding records `job_binding_id` and `release_hash` on the run; an internal-agent binding records its pinned agent.
- `industries.*`, `departments.*`, `job_catalogue.*`, `job_releases.*` and `job_bindings.*` are served with the new `organisation:read` and `organisation:write` scopes; each action is one `ActionSpec` over HTTP and MCP, and `served-spec.lock.json` matches the registry.
- A binding with neither executor is refused `422`; a viewer publishing a release is refused `403` with no row written.
- The decision-ladder types — `decision`, `decision_option`, `decision_policy`, `decision_policy_refinement`, `laya_inference_config` — exist as schema and contracts with FORCE RLS, and no evaluation path exists yet.
- The internal `Executor` contract lives in `crates/domain/src/executor.rs` with `procedure` and `internal_agent` implementations; a test-only third kind registers without touching the run path.
- `seed/organisation.json` loads idempotently: three industries (software, health-technology-assessment, media), the five ordered software departments (delivery, verification, operations, project_office, improvement) and 22 jobs — the five fully described jobs plus the SPEC §4.6 drafts.
- `conveyor snapshot` populates `organisation.json` for a seeded tenant with no secret value or email; the Organisation design page renders the live rows with a LIVE ribbon.
- The project closes through the one gate: charter approved, baseline approved, board-approved delivery contract with an approver distinct from the requester, compliant Phase-G review citing the published standing delegation, closure gate decided by a distinct approver, 0 waivers, 1 WBS node with the four WSJF inputs and 1 accepted deliverable with a demo credit.

## Verify commands

- `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test organisation` — `organisation_tables_are_forced_rls`, `job_departments_are_ordered_and_placement_is_validated`, `release_hash_is_deterministic_and_publish_is_idempotent`, `a_binding_must_agree_with_the_release_executor`, `a_run_pins_its_binding_and_a_retired_or_mismatched_pin_is_refused`, `third_executor_kind_registers_without_editing_the_run_path`, `seed_organisation_is_idempotent_and_the_seeded_anatomy_compiles`.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test organisation_gate` — `run_on_a_retired_binding_is_refused_409_before_the_insert`, `a_run_on_an_internal_agent_binding_records_its_pinned_agent`, `a_run_without_a_binding_records_no_agent`, `a_binding_without_an_executor_is_422_and_a_viewer_is_403`.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test registry --test parity_http_mcp` — the organisation actions and the lock parity.
- `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test snapshot_deterministic organisation_is_populated_for_a_seeded_tenant`.
- `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs`.
- `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project T0` — the manifest `acceptance/programme/T0.toml`.

## Results

Met. PR #65, "feat(organisation): T0 — the organisation spine", merged `1f48e2685e333ef2f6704e677afaae9f80e664f1` on 2026-11-14T18:40:13Z and closed #34 as COMPLETED at 18:40:15Z. The merge carried `migrations/0040_organisation.sql`, `seed/organisation.json`, `crates/domain/src/executor.rs`, the store, actions and server tests, and the regenerated `served-spec.lock.json`; 41 files in total. The tranche-0 retrospective rework re-verified the project on 2026-11-26: verdict green at snapshot `7f0df874e7c26681ee36923b5c17e76a99254b24`, 14 checks pass, 0 failures, 0 active waivers, 1 closure output published, PI cadence and refinement rows for tranche-0, 1 WBS node with the four WSJF inputs, and 1 accepted deliverable with a demo credit. The 2026-11-14 closure had no contemporaneous charter, SoAW, delivery contract, Phase-G review or closure review; the rework authored and evidenced that governance chain, with the contract approver and the closure-gate approver distinct from the requester.

## Status

met — the organisation spine and the Executor seam are on `main`; the project re-closed green on 2026-11-26. Decision evaluation and decision behaviour are T2's, not carry-over from T0.

## Links

- Issue #34; PR #65; `docs/evidence/rework/T0.json`; `acceptance/programme/T0.toml`.
- Spec: `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §4.1–§4.6, §10.3–§10.5, §12 T0.

documents.body:
# Definition of ready — Model and contracts (T0)

## Independent

T0 heads the dependency chain. Its only blocked-by, #57, merged `7919b8e`, and the T0 board, its card and the process catalogue were live before the claim; T1, T2 and T3 are blocked by T0 (SPEC §12). The six parts — schema, release hash and stale refusal, actions, seed, snapshot, decision types and the Executor seam — land in one branch and one PR. The deliberately shared seam, `insert_run_tx` and the domain `Run`, is where the pin recording and the stale refusal must sit; it is not a second concept.

## Negotiable

The outcome is fixed: the organisation spine as real rows, the immutable release pinned by a binding, the stale refusal, the decision-ladder types and the Executor seam. The shape was settled at delivery. The V1 `procedure` table was already `process`, and the new `procedure` is the SOP. The migration renumbered from the expected 39 to `0040_organisation.sql` because `0039_document_outputs.sql` took the slot. The planned `organisation_authz.rs` viewer test landed as the 403 arm of `a_binding_without_an_executor_is_422_and_a_viewer_is_403` instead.

## Valuable

T0 removes the named gap. Before it, no `industry`, `job_catalogue`, `job_release` or `job_binding` existed, `run` had no binding, and the snapshot's `organisation.json` published empty arrays. T0 installs the organisation spine the SPEC §12 sequence puts first, with D40's rule that no aggregate ships without a named procedure and a metric, and it lands the Executor seam D61 requires. It unblocks T1, T2 and T3.

## Estimable

Baseline `origin/main@5f584e3`, measured 2026-11-13. The issue names every file and test target: the five tables and the `run` columns, the canonical-snapshot rule, the action families with `organisation:read` and `organisation:write`, the three seed industries, the five ordered software departments and the five fully described jobs. The design source `docs/design/v2.js` F.industries/departments/jobs/releases/bindings is pinned to #32, closed.

## Small

One issue (#34), one branch and one PR (#65): 41 files across the store, domain, actions, server and design-data surfaces. Decision evaluation and behaviour are explicitly T2's; T0 ships the five decision tables as schema and contracts only. No second app or cluster surface is touched.

## Testable

Every part carries a Given/When/Then scenario with a named test: `crates/store/tests/organisation.rs`, `apps/server/tests/organisation_gate.rs`, `apps/server/tests/snapshot_deterministic.rs`, the actions registry and parity tests, and `docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs`. The project-level test is the acceptance manifest `acceptance/programme/T0.toml`, run by `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project T0`.

## Dependencies

- blocked-by: #57 — merged `7919b8e`; the T0 board, its card and the process catalogue were live.
- related: #33 — the live build surface whose snapshot section publishes `organisation.json`; #24 — SPEC V2 landed on `main`; #32 — the design source, closed.
- blocks: T1, T2 and T3 — the organisation spine is their prerequisite (SPEC §12).
- external: none — no third-party call is needed to satisfy T0.

## Notes

Reconstructed for standard v4 on 2026-11-28 from the issue's Definition of Ready and the merged record. All five boxes were checked at claim. The one residual is procedural: the 2026-11-14 closure's governance paperwork was reconstructed in the 2026-11-26 rework.

documents.body:
# Definition of done — Model and contracts (T0)

## Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Verify |
|---|---|
| The five spine tables and the extended `department` exist with FORCE RLS; `run.job_binding_id` and `run.release_hash` are nullable | `organisation_tables_are_forced_rls`; `job_departments_are_ordered_and_placement_is_validated` |
| The release hash is deterministic over the canonical snapshot and publish is idempotent | `release_hash_is_deterministic_and_publish_is_idempotent` |
| A binding agrees with its release's executor anatomy | `a_binding_must_agree_with_the_release_executor` |
| A retired or mismatched binding is refused `409 job_binding_stale` before the insert, naming both hashes, with no row written | `run_on_a_retired_binding_is_refused_409_before_the_insert`; `a_run_pins_its_binding_and_a_retired_or_mismatched_pin_is_refused` |
| An active binding pins `job_binding_id` and `release_hash` on the run | `a_run_on_an_internal_agent_binding_records_its_pinned_agent`; `a_run_without_a_binding_records_no_agent` |
| A binding with no executor is `422`; a viewer publish is `403` and writes no row | `a_binding_without_an_executor_is_422_and_a_viewer_is_403` |
| Every organisation action is one `ActionSpec` over HTTP and MCP, with `served-spec.lock.json` matching | `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test registry --test parity_http_mcp` |
| A test-only third executor kind registers without editing the run path | `third_executor_kind_registers_without_editing_the_run_path` |
| The five decision tables exist with FORCE RLS and no evaluation path | `migrations/0040_organisation.sql`; the registry carries no decision evaluation action |
| The seed is idempotent and the seeded anatomy compiles | `seed_organisation_is_idempotent_and_the_seeded_anatomy_compiles` |
| `organisation.json` is populated for a seeded tenant | `organisation_is_populated_for_a_seeded_tenant` |
| The design site renders the live rows | `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs` |
| The project closes through the one gate | `acceptance/programme/T0.toml`; `docs/evidence/rework/T0.json` |

## Evidence at completion

PR #65 merged `1f48e2685e333ef2f6704e677afaae9f80e664f1` on 2026-11-14T18:40:13Z and closed #34 as COMPLETED at 18:40:15Z. The tree carries `migrations/0040_organisation.sql`, `seed/organisation.json`, `crates/domain/src/executor.rs`, `crates/store/src/organisation.rs`, `crates/actions/src/organisation.rs`, the organisation, gate and snapshot tests, and the regenerated `served-spec.lock.json`. `crates/store/src/migrate.rs` carries `(40, "organisation")`.

The rework record `docs/evidence/rework/T0.json` is green at snapshot `7f0df874e7c26681ee36923b5c17e76a99254b24` (2026-11-26): baseline approved; charter gate approved; 1 closure output published; delivery contract board-approved by an approver distinct from the requester; Phase-G review compliant and citing the published standing delegation; closure gate decided by a distinct approver; 0 active waivers; PI cadence and refinement rows for tranche-0; 1 WBS node with the four WSJF inputs; 1 accepted deliverable with a demo credit; no open P0 product finding; no open standard artefact package; no unresolved P0/P1 rework package; 14 checks pass, 0 failures.

At the 2026-11-14 closure the original charter, SoAW, delivery contract, Phase-G review and closure review had not been authored; the contemporaneous record was evidence document `01a1e688-678d-76fd-8ae7-6ca2712b64c2` and the git history. The 2026-11-26 rework authored and evidenced the governance chain above.

## Repo gate

The unit gate: `cargo test -p conveyor-store --test organisation`, `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test organisation_gate`, `cargo test -p conveyor-server --test snapshot_deterministic`, `cargo test -p conveyor-actions --test registry --test parity_http_mcp`, and `node docs/design/scripts/check-data.cjs`. The embedded migration-set test in `crates/store/src/migrate.rs` carries `(40, "organisation")`. The historical issue's P3.1 names `rbuild`; that route is retired, and the compile and lint verdict is the repository's preflight and the PR's CI. The project gate is `python3 scripts/verify-project.py --project T0`.

## Merge and closure

One unit of work: issue #34, one branch, one non-draft PR #65, merged 2026-11-14T18:40:13Z, with the issue closed COMPLETED at 18:40:15Z. The tranche-0 retrospective rework re-verified the project on 2026-11-26, and the verdict green at snapshot `7f0df874e7c26681ee36923b5c17e76a99254b24` is the closure evidence. No waiver was taken.

## Links

- Issue #34; PR #65; `docs/evidence/rework/T0.json` and `docs/evidence/rework/T0.md`; `acceptance/programme/T0.toml`.
- Spec: `docs/SPEC_V2.md` §4.1–§4.6, §10.3–§10.5, §12 T0; D38, D40, D60, D61.
